# Doxygen

Doxygen is the de facto standard tool for generating documentation from
annotated C++ sources, but it also supports other popular programming
languages such as C, Objective-C, C#, PHP, Java, Python, IDL
(Corba, Microsoft, and UNO/OpenOffice flavors), Fortran,
and to some extent D. Doxygen also supports the hardware description language VHDL.

## What Doxygen Does

Doxygen can help you in three ways:

1. It can generate an online documentation browser (in HTML) and/or an
   offline reference manual (in LaTeX) from a set of documented source files.
   There is also support for generating output in RTF (MS-Word), PostScript,
   hyperlinked PDF, compressed HTML, DocBook and Unix man pages.
   The documentation is extracted directly from the sources, which makes
   it much easier to keep the documentation consistent with the source code.

2. You can configure doxygen to extract the code structure from undocumented
   source files. This is very useful to quickly find your way in large
   source distributions. Doxygen can also visualize the relations between
   the various elements by means of include dependency graphs, inheritance
   diagrams, and collaboration diagrams, which are all generated automatically.

3. You can also use doxygen for creating normal documentation (as I did for
   the doxygen user manual and doxygen website).

## Usage

Doxygen is a command line based utility. Here are the main ways to use it:

### 1) Generate a template configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -g [configName]
```

### 2) Update an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [-s] -u [configName]
```

### 3) Generate documentation using an existing configuration file

```bash
doxygen [configName]
```

### 4) Generate a template file that controls the layout of the generated documentation

```bash
doxygen -l [layoutFileName]
```

If layoutFileName is omitted, DoxygenLayout.xml will be used as the filename.
If - is used for layoutFileName, Doxygen writes to standard output.

### 5) Generate a template style sheet file for RTF, HTML or LaTeX

For RTF:
```bash
doxygen -w rtf styleSheetFile
```

For HTML:
```bash
doxygen -w html headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

For LaTeX:
```bash
doxygen -w latex headerFile footerFile styleSheetFile [configFile]
```

import subprocess, os, tempfile
def run(cfg_text, args=None, extra_files=None, label=""):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    if extra_files:
        for k,v in extra_files.items():
            p=os.path.join(d,k); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True) if os.path.dirname(k) else None
            open(p,"w").write(v)
    open(os.path.join(d,"Doxyfile"),"w").write(cfg_text)
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+(args or ["Doxyfile"]), cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print("===",label)
    print("cfg:",repr(cfg_text))
    print("exit",p.returncode)
    print("out:",p.stdout[:2000])
    print("err:",p.stderr[:2000])
    print("files:",sorted([os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r,f),d) for r,_,fs in os.walk(d) for f in fs]))
    print()
    return d,p

import subprocess, os, tempfile, hashlib
def harvest(cfg):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    if cfg is not None:
        open(os.path.join(d,"cfg"),"w").write(cfg)
        args=["/workspace/executable","-w","html","h","f","s","cfg"]
    else:
        args=["/workspace/executable","-w","html","h","f","s"]
    p=subprocess.run(args,cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True)
    res={}
    for fn in ["h","f","s"]:
        fp=os.path.join(d,fn)
        res[fn]=hashlib.md5(open(fp,'rb').read()).hexdigest() if os.path.exists(fp) else None
    print(repr(cfg), p.returncode, res, repr(p.stderr[:500]), repr(p.stdout[:200]))
    if cfg:
        # show diff head vs default
        pass
    return d
d0=harvest(None)
d1=harvest("PROJECT_NAME = Foo\nHTML_COLORSTYLE_HUE = 100\n")
d2=harvest("GENERATE_TREEVIEW = YES\n")
d3=harvest("HTML_DYNAMIC_MENUS = NO\nDISABLE_INDEX = YES\n")
d4=harvest("UNKNOWN = 1\n")
# diff files
import difflib
for fn in ["h","f","s"]:
    a=open(os.path.join(d0,fn)).readlines(); b=open(os.path.join(d1,fn)).readlines()
    diff=list(difflib.unified_diff(a,b))
    print(fn,"diff vs hue",len(diff)); print(''.join(diff[:40]))
for fn in ["h","f","s"]:
    a=open(os.path.join(d0,fn)).readlines(); b=open(os.path.join(d2,fn)).readlines()
    diff=list(difflib.unified_diff(a,b)); print(fn,"diff vs treeview",len(diff)); print(''.join(diff[:40]))
# latex with cfg
def harvestL(cfg):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    if cfg is not None:
        open(os.path.join(d,"cfg"),"w").write(cfg); args=["/workspace/executable","-w","latex","h","f","s","cfg"]
    else: args=["/workspace/executable","-w","latex","h","f","s"]
    p=subprocess.run(args,cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True)
    print("latex",repr(cfg),p.returncode,{fn:(os.path.getsize(os.path.join(d,fn)) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d,fn)) else None) for fn in ["h","f","s"]},repr(p.stderr[:300]))
    return d
l0=harvestL(None); l1=harvestL("PAPER_TYPE = a4\nLATEX_BATCHMODE = YES\nPDF_HYPERLINKS = NO\n")
for fn in ["h","f","s"]:
    a=open(os.path.join(l0,fn)).readlines(); b=open(os.path.join(l1,fn)).readlines()
    diff=list(difflib.unified_diff(a,b)); print("latex",fn,len(diff)); print(''.join(diff[:60]))
# rtf -w with ??? does it accept config? extra ignored earlier
PY"}

    x(f"OUTPUT_LANGUAGE = {v}\n")
# enum value representation

    x(f"PAPER_TYPE = {v}\n")

# obsolete candidates quick
for tag in ["HTML_TIMESTAMP","LATEX_TIMESTAMP","RTF_TIMESTAMP","MAN_TIMESTAMP","XML_TIMESTAMP","SHOW_FILES","SHOW_NAMESPACES","USE_WINDOWS_ENCODING","DETAILS_AT_TOP","QTHELP_FILE","GENERATE_QTHELP","USE_HTAGS","SYMBOL_CACHE_SIZE","XML_SCHEMA","XML_DTD"]:

import subprocess, tempfile, os, re, json
tags=[]
defaults={}
# parse short template including continuations
text=open('/tmp/harvest/doxyfile_short.txt').read()
# join continuation lines: lines ending with backslash
raw=text.splitlines()
joined=[]; buf=""
for l in raw:
    if buf: buf+= "\n"+l
    else: buf=l
    if l.rstrip().endswith("\\"):
        continue
    joined.append(buf); buf=""
for l in joined:
    m=re.match(r'^([A-Z0-9_]+)\s*=\s?(.*)$',l,re.S)
    if m:
        tags.append(m.group(1)); defaults[m.group(1)]=m.group(2)
print("tags",len(tags))

def x(cfg):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); open(os.path.join(d,"Doxyfile"),"w").write(cfg)
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-x","Doxyfile"],cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True)
    return p.stdout.splitlines()[1:], p.stderr

info={}
for t in tags:
    diff,err=x(f"{t} = BOGUS_VALUE_XYZ123\n")
    typ="string_or_list"
    rng=None
    if "not a valid boolean" in err: typ="bool"
    elif "not a valid number" in err:
        typ="int"; m=re.search(r"range \[([^\]]+)\]",err); rng=m.group(1) if m else None
    elif "not a valid enum" in err: typ="enum"
    elif err: typ="other:"+err.strip().splitlines()[0]
    info[t]={"type":typ,"range":rng,"default_raw":defaults[t],"bogus_diff":diff,"bogus_err":err}
    # distinguish string/list using two words
    if typ=="string_or_list":
        diff2,err2=x(f"{t} = AAA BBB\n")
        # list will produce continuation lines; string produces quoted "AAA BBB"
        if len(diff2)>1 or (diff2 and diff2[0].rstrip().endswith("\\")):
            info[t]["type"]="list"
        else:
            info[t]["type"]="string"
        info[t]["twoword_diff"]=diff2
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(v["type"] for v in info.values()))
for t,v in info.items():
    if v["type"] not in ("bool","string","list"):
        print(t,v["type"],v["range"],repr(v["default_raw"]))

"""Helpers for writing generated/template files."""

import os
import sys


def backup_existing(path):
    """If ``path`` exists, rename it to ``path.bak`` (as the reference
    does for all template-writing commands)."""
    if os.path.lexists(path):
        try:
            os.replace(path, path + ".bak")
        except OSError:
            # e.g. renaming a file onto a non-empty directory: the
            # subsequent open() will report the failure.
            pass


def write_template_file(path, content):
    """Write text/bytes ``content`` to ``path`` (or stdout for '-').

    Returns True on success.  Existing files are backed up first."""
    if path == "-":
        if isinstance(content, bytes):
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(content)
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(content)
        return True
    backup_existing(path)
    try:
        if isinstance(content, bytes):
            with open(path, "wb") as fh:
                fh.write(content)
        else:
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
                fh.write(content)
    except OSError:
        return False
    return True


def write_output_file(path, content):
    """Write a generated documentation file (no backup)."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
    if directory:
        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
    if isinstance(content, bytes):
        with open(path, "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(content)
    else:
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
            fh.write(content)

import subprocess,tempfile,os,sys,hashlib,shutil
REF="/workspace/executable"; MINE="/tmp/mybuild/executable"
def run_one(exe,args,files,inp,env_extra):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    if files:
        for k,v in files.items():
            p=os.path.join(d,k)
            if '/' in k: os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True)
            if isinstance(v,bytes): open(p,"wb").write(v)
            else: open(p,"w").write(v)
    e=dict(os.environ); e.update(env_extra or {})
    p=subprocess.run([exe]+args,cwd=d,input=inp,capture_output=True,env=e)
    filemap={}
    for r,_,fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            fp=os.path.join(r,f); rel=os.path.relpath(fp,d)
            filemap[rel]=open(fp,"rb").read()
    # remove input known files? keep for comparison incl modifications
    return p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr,filemap,d
def compare(args,files=None,inp=None,env=None,label=""):
    # normalise argv0 difference in help: run both via same relative name? copy/symlink executables as ./executable in workdir would taint files list. Instead replace exe path strings in outputs.
    r=run_one(REF,args,files,inp,env); m=run_one(MINE,args,files,inp,env)
    def norm(b,exe):
        return b.replace(exe.encode(),b"./executable")
    ok=True; msgs=[]
    if r[0]!=m[0]: ok=False; msgs.append(f"exit ref={r[0]} mine={m[0]}")
    if norm(r[1],REF)!=norm(m[1],MINE): ok=False; msgs.append(f"stdout ref={norm(r[1],REF)[:300]!r} mine={norm(m[1],MINE)[:300]!r}")
    if norm(r[2],REF)!=norm(m[2],MINE): ok=False; msgs.append(f"stderr ref={r[2][:400]!r} mine={m[2][:400]!r}")
    # files: compare sets and content, but temp abs paths can occur in some generated files (perlmod etc) - for current tests none
    rf,mf=r[3],m[3]
    if set(rf)!=set(mf): ok=False; msgs.append(f"files ref={sorted(rf)} mine={sorted(mf)}")
    else:
        for k in rf:
            if rf[k]!=mf[k]:
                # find first diff
                a,b=rf[k],mf[k]; idx=next((i for i in range(min(len(a),len(b))) if a[i]!=b[i]),min(len(a),len(b)))
                ok=False; msgs.append(f"file {k} differs len {len(a)} vs {len(b)} at {idx}: ref={a[max(0,idx-60):idx+80]!r} mine={b[max(0,idx-60):idx+80]!r}")
                break
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ")+(label or " ".join(args)))
    for msg in msgs: print("   ",msg)
    return ok

if __name__=="__main__":
    pass

"""Parsing of documentation comment blocks into a small block/inline
tree that the output generators can render.

Inline nodes are tuples whose first element is a tag:

    ("heading", level, id, title_nodes)

import re

CMD_RE = re.compile(r"[@\\]([A-Za-z]+)")

# Commands that start a "simple section" in the detailed description.
SIMPLESECT_KINDS = {

    "warning": "warning", "attention": "attention",

    "todo": "todo", "test": "test", "bug": "bug",
    "deprecated": "deprecated",
    "satisfies": "satisfies", "verifies": "verifies",
}

KNOWN_COMMANDS = set(SIMPLESECT_KINDS) | {
    "brief", "details", "detail", "short",
    "param", "tparam", "retval", "exception", "throw", "throws",
    "section", "subsection", "subsubsection", "paragraph", "subpage",
    "code", "endcode", "verbatim", "endverbatim",
    "htmlonly", "endhtmlonly", "manonly", "endmanonly",
    "latexonly", "endlatexonly", "rtfonly", "endrtfonly",
    "xmlonly", "endxmlonly", "docbookonly", "enddocbookonly",
    "c", "p", "b", "e", "em", "a", "ref", "link", "endlink", "n",
    "file", "class", "struct", "union", "namespace", "interface",
    "protocol", "category", "concept", "defgroup", "addtogroup",
    "weakgroup", "page", "mainpage", "fn", "var", "typedef", "enum",
    "package", "module", "dir", "example", "topic", "overload",
    "ingroup", "name", "memberof", "relates", "relatesalso",
    "callgraph", "callergraph", "hidecallgraph", "hidecallergraph",
    "inheritancegraph", "hideinheritancegraph", "showinit", "hideinit",
    "internal", "endinternal", "cond", "endcond", "if", "ifnot", "else", "elif", "endif",
    "li", "snippet", "include", "includelineno", "line", "skipline",
    "skip", "until", "dontinclude", "image", "dot", "enddot", "msc", "endmsc",
    "startuml", "enduml", "anchor", "addindex", "id", "tableofcontents",
    "copyright", "addtogroup", "weakgroup", "noop", "lineinfo",
    "arg", "throws", "f$", "f[", "f]", "f{", "f}", "emoji",
}

STRUCTURAL_COMMANDS = {
    "file", "class", "struct", "union", "namespace", "interface",
    "protocol", "category", "concept", "defgroup", "addtogroup",
    "weakgroup", "page", "mainpage", "fn", "var", "typedef", "enum",
    "package", "module", "dir", "example", "topic",
}


class Doc:
    def __init__(self):
        self.brief = []      # list of blocks
        self.detailed = []   # list of blocks
        self.inbody = []
        self.structural = None   # (command, args string)
        self.ingroups = []
        self.is_brief_explicit = False
        self.has_doc = False

    def empty(self):
        return not self.brief and not self.detailed and not self.inbody

    def text_of(self, which="brief"):
        blocks = self.brief if which == "brief" else self.detailed
        return blocks_to_text(blocks).strip()


def inline_to_text(nodes):
    out = []
    for n in nodes:
        tag = n[0]
        if tag == "text":
            out.append(n[1])
        elif tag == "code":
            out.append(n[1])
        elif tag in ("bold", "emph"):
            out.append(inline_to_text(n[1]))
        elif tag == "ref":
            out.append(inline_to_text(n[2]) if len(n) > 2 and n[2] else n[1])
        elif tag == "link":
            out.append(inline_to_text(n[2]))
        elif tag == "break":
            out.append("\n")
    return "".join(out)


def blocks_to_text(blocks):
    out = []
    for b in blocks:
        tag = b[0]
        if tag == "para":
            out.append(inline_to_text(b[1]))
        elif tag == "simplesect":
            out.append(blocks_to_text(b[2]))
        elif tag == "paramlist":
            for names, desc in b[2]:
                out.append(blocks_to_text(desc))
        elif tag in ("codeblock", "verbatim"):
            out.append(b[1])
        elif tag == "list":
            for item in b[2]:
                out.append(blocks_to_text(item))
        elif tag == "sect":
            out.append(inline_to_text(b[3]))
            out.append(blocks_to_text(b[4]))
        elif tag == "only":
            out.append(blocks_to_text(b[2]))
    return "\n".join(x for x in out if x)


def _read_word(text, i):
    """Read the next whitespace-delimited word; return (word, new_index)."""
    n = len(text)
    while i < n and text[i] in " \t":
        i += 1
    start = i
    while i < n and text[i] not in " \t\n":
        i += 1
    return text[start:i], i


def _read_line(text, i):
    n = len(text)
    start = i
    while i < n and text[i] != "\n":
        i += 1
    return text[start:i], i


class _InlineParser:
    def __init__(self, text, warn, fileline):
        self.text = text
        self.warn = warn
        self.fileline = fileline  # (file, start_line)

    def warn_unknown(self, cmd, pos):
        if self.warn:
            line = self.fileline[1] + self.text[:pos].count("\n")
            self.warn(
                f"{self.fileline[0]}:{line}: warning: Found unknown command '{cmd}'\n"
            )

    def parse(self, start=0, end=None, stop_cmd=None):
        """Parse inline content.  Returns (nodes, index) where index is at
        the stopping command/paragraph end if any."""
        text = self.text
        n = len(text) if end is None else end
        nodes = []
        buf = []

        def flush():
            if buf:
                nodes.append(("text", "".join(buf)))
                buf.clear()

        i = start
        while i < n:
            ch = text[i]
            if ch in "@\\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1].isalpha():
                m = CMD_RE.match(text, i)
                if m:
                    cmd = m.group(1).lower()
                    cmd_text = text[i:m.end()]
                    if stop_cmd and cmd == stop_cmd:
                        flush()
                        return nodes, i
                    if cmd in ("c", "p"):
                        flush()
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        nodes.append(("code", word.strip(".,;:") if word.endswith(".") and cmd == "p" else word))
                        # The punctuation handling above is intentionally
                        # simple; see below for the '.' that trails a \p.
                        if word.endswith("."):
                            # Re-emit trailing punctuation as text when the
                            # word was 'paramref.' at the end of a sentence.
                            pass
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "b":
                        flush()
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        nodes.append(("bold", [("text", word)]))
                        continue
                    elif cmd in ("e", "em", "a"):
                        flush()
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        nodes.append(("emph", [("text", word)]))
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "n":
                        flush()
                        nodes.append(("break",))
                        i = m.end()
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "ref":
                        flush()
                        # \ref target ["text"]
                        j = m.end()
                        while j < n and text[j] in " \t":
                            j += 1
                        if j < n and text[j] == '"':
                            # \ref "text" form is not standard; treat word.
                            pass
                        target, j = _read_word(text, j)
                        # Optional quoted display text.
                        k = j
                        while k < n and text[k] in " \t":
                            k += 1
                        display = None
                        if k < n and text[k] == '"':
                            e = text.find('"', k + 1)
                            if e != -1 and e <= n:
                                display = text[k + 1:e]
                                j = e + 1
                        nodes.append(("ref", target, [("text", display)] if display else None))
                        i = j
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "link":
                        flush()
                        target, j = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        inner, j2 = self.parse(j, n, stop_cmd="endlink")
                        nodes.append(("ref", target, inner))
                        i = j2
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "endlink":
                        flush()
                        return nodes, i
                    elif cmd == "emoji":
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        buf.append(f":{word}:")
                        continue
                    elif cmd in KNOWN_COMMANDS:
                        # A known command that is not handled inline;
                        # let the block parser deal with it by stopping.
                        flush()
                        return nodes, i
                    else:
                        self.warn_unknown(cmd_text, i)
                        buf.append(cmd_text)
                        i = m.end()
                        continue
            if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < n and not text[i + 1].isalpha():
                # Escaped special character.
                buf.append(text[i + 1])
                i += 2
                continue
            if ch == "@" and i + 1 < n and not text[i + 1].isalpha():
                buf.append(text[i + 1] if text[i + 1] in "@\\$&%\"#." else "@")
                i += 2 if text[i + 1] in "@\\$&%\"#." else 1
                continue
            buf.append(ch)
            i += 1
        flush()
        return nodes, i


def parse_inline(text, warn=None, fileline=("", 1)):
    return _InlineParser(text, warn, fileline).parse(0)[0]


def _split_paragraphs(text):
    """Split text into paragraph strings separated by blank lines."""
    paras = []
    cur = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if line.strip() == "":
            if cur:
                paras.append("\n".join(cur))
                cur = []
        else:
            cur.append(line)
    if cur:
        paras.append("\n".join(cur))
    return paras


def apply_markdown_inline(nodes):
    """Apply lightweight Markdown emphasis/code/link processing to text
    nodes (used both for Markdown files and markup in comments)."""
    out = []
    for node in nodes:
        if node[0] != "text":
            out.append(node)
            continue
        s = node[1]
        # Process `code`, **bold**, *emph*, [text](url) in a single scan.
        i = 0
        buf = []

        def flush():
            if buf:
                out.append(("text", "".join(buf)))
                buf.clear()

        while i < len(s):
            if s.startswith("`", i):
                j = s.find("`", i + 1)
                if j != -1:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("code", s[i + 1:j]))
                    i = j + 1
                    continue
            if s.startswith("**", i) or s.startswith("__", i):
                marker = s[i:i + 2]
                j = s.find(marker, i + 2)
                if j != -1:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("bold", [("text", s[i + 2:j])]))
                    i = j + 2
                    continue
            if s[i] in "*_" and i + 1 < len(s) and not s[i + 1].isspace():
                j = s.find(s[i], i + 1)
                if j != -1 and j > i + 1:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("emph", [("text", s[i + 1:j])]))
                    i = j + 1
                    continue
            if s[i] == "[":
                m = re.match(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)\s]+)[^)]*\)", s[i:])
                if m:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("link", m.group(2), [("text", m.group(1))]))
                    i += m.end()
                    continue
            buf.append(s[i])
            i += 1
        flush()
    return out


class DocParser:
    def __init__(self, cfg, warn=None, filename="", start_line=1):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.warn = warn
        self.filename = filename
        self.start_line = start_line

    def _warn(self, msg):
        if self.warn:
            self.warn(msg)

    def _inline(self, text):
        idx_parser = _InlineParser(text, self._warn,
                                    (self.filename, self.start_line))
        nodes, _ = idx_parser.parse(0)
        if self.cfg is None or self.cfg.get_bool("MARKDOWN_SUPPORT"):
            nodes = apply_markdown_inline(nodes)
        # Merge adjacent text nodes and normalise whitespace runs
        # (keeping single spaces).
        merged = []
        for node in nodes:
            if node[0] == "text":
                txt = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", node[1])
                if merged and merged[-1][0] == "text":
                    merged[-1] = ("text", merged[-1][1] + txt)
                else:
                    merged.append(("text", txt))
            else:
                merged.append(node)
        return merged

    def parse(self, text, style="block", trailing=False):
        """style: one of 'block', 'line', 'qt', 'lineqt', 'python'."""
        doc = Doc()
        original = text
        text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

        # Extract \ingroup commands (removing them from the text).
        def repl_ingroup(m):
            doc.ingroups.extend(m.group(1).split())
            return ""
        text = re.sub(r"[@\\]ingroup\s+([^\n]*)", repl_ingroup, text)
        text = re.sub(r"[@\\]memberof\s+([^\n]*)", "", text)

        # Structural command: only when it is the first command in the block.
        stripped = text.lstrip(" \t\n")
        m = CMD_RE.match(stripped)
        if m and m.group(1).lower() in STRUCTURAL_COMMANDS:
            cmd = m.group(1).lower()
            rest, _ = _read_line(stripped, m.end())
            doc.structural = (cmd, rest.strip())
            # Remove the command and its line-rest from the text.
            first_nl = stripped.find("\n", m.end())
            if first_nl == -1:
                text = ""
            else:
                text = stripped[first_nl + 1:]
            if cmd == "defgroup" or cmd in ("addtogroup", "weakgroup"):
                pass

        doc.has_doc = bool(original.strip()) or doc.structural is not None

        # Determine explicit brief.
        has_brief = bool(re.search(r"[@\\](brief|short)\b", text))

        blocks_detailed = []
        blocks_brief = []

        # paragraph.  We walk the whole text with a state machine over
        # "segments": (text chunk between block commands).
        detailed = self._parse_blocks(text, doc, allow_brief=has_brief)

        blocks_detailed = detailed.get("detailed", [])

        # Implicit brief handling.
        if not has_brief and not blocks_brief:
            mode = self._implicit_brief(style, trailing)
            if mode == "all":
                blocks_brief, blocks_detailed = blocks_detailed, []
            elif mode == "first-para" and blocks_detailed:
                if blocks_detailed[0][0] == "para":
                    blocks_brief = [blocks_detailed.pop(0)]
            elif mode == "first-sentence" and blocks_detailed:
                if blocks_detailed[0][0] == "para":
                    first, rest = _split_first_sentence(blocks_detailed[0][1])
                    if first is not None and rest is not None:
                        blocks_brief = [("para", first)]
                        if rest:
                            blocks_detailed[0] = ("para", rest)
                        else:
                            blocks_detailed.pop(0)
                    else:
                        blocks_brief = [blocks_detailed.pop(0)]

        doc.detailed = blocks_detailed
        return doc

    def _implicit_brief(self, style, trailing):
        cfg = self.cfg
        if cfg is None:
            return "all" if style in ("line", "lineqt") and not trailing else None
        javadoc = cfg.get_bool("JAVADOC_AUTOBRIEF")
        qt = cfg.get_bool("QT_AUTOBRIEF")
        is_qt_style = style in ("qt", "lineqt")
        is_javadoc_style = style in ("block", "line")
        if javadoc or qt:
            if (is_javadoc_style and javadoc) or (is_qt_style and qt):
                return "first-sentence"
            return None
        if style in ("line", "lineqt"):
            if cfg.get_bool("MULTILINE_CPP_IS_BRIEF"):
                return "first-para"
            return "single-para-all"
        return None

    def _parse_blocks(self, text, doc, allow_brief):
        """Returns {"brief": [...], "detailed": [...]}."""

        root = []

        current_para_text = []

        brief_done = False

        container_stack = []

        def flush_para():

            current_para_text = []
            if txt.strip() == "":
                return

            target.extend(blocks)

        # start of a segment below.

                        e = text.find("]", j)
                        if e != -1:
                            direction = text[j + 1:e].strip()
                            j = e + 1

                    while True:
                        w, j2 = _read_word(text, j)
                        if not w:
                            break
                        names.extend([x for x in re.split(r",", w) if x])
                        j = j2
                        # comma separated more names?
                        k = j
                        while k < n and text[k] in " \t":
                            k += 1
                        if k < n and text[k] == ",":
                            j = k + 1
                            continue
                        break
                    kind_list = "param"
                    pos = j
                else:
                    w, pos = _read_word(text, cend)
                    names = [w] if w else []
                    kind_list = {
                        "tparam": "templateparam",
                        "retval": "retval",
                        "exception": "exception",
                        "throw": "exception",
                        "throws": "exception",
                    }[lname]
                    direction = None
                # Find existing trailing paramlist of same kind to append.
                target = container if container is not None else root
                # Close any simplesect container first.
                if container_stack:
                    while container_stack:
                        container = container_stack.pop()
                    target = container
                if target and target[-1][0] == "paramlist" and target[-1][1] == kind_list:
                    plist = target[-1][2]
                else:
                    plist = []
                    target.append(("paramlist", kind_list, plist))
                desc = []
                named = [(nm, direction) for nm in names] if direction else [(nm, None) for nm in names]
                plist.append((named, desc))
                container_stack.append(target)
                container = desc
                continue
            if lname in SIMPLESECT_KINDS:
                flush_para()
                in_brief = False
                kind_sect = SIMPLESECT_KINDS[lname]
                if container_stack:
                    while container_stack:
                        container = container_stack.pop()
                target = container
                inner = []
                target.append(("simplesect", kind_sect, inner))
                container_stack.append(target)
                container = inner
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in ("section", "subsection", "subsubsection", "paragraph"):
                flush_para()
                in_brief = False
                level = {"section": 1, "subsection": 2, "subsubsection": 3, "paragraph": 4}[lname]
                sid, j = _read_word(text, cend)
                title, j2 = _read_line(text, j)
                if not sid and title:
                    sid = ""
                if container_stack:
                    while container_stack:
                        container = container_stack.pop()
                inner = []
                container.append(("sect", level, sid, self._inline(title.strip()), inner))
                container_stack.append(container)
                container = inner
                pos = j2
                continue
            if lname in ("code", "verbatim"):
                flush_para()
                endcmd = "endcode" if lname == "code" else "endverbatim"
                # Optional {language} or .ext after \code
                j = cend
                lang = ""
                mj = re.match(r"\s*\{([^}]*)\}|\s*\.([A-Za-z0-9_]+)", text[j:j+40])
                if mj:
                    lang = mj.group(1) or mj.group(2) or ""
                    j += mj.end()
                e = self._find_command(text, endcmd, j)
                code_text = text[j:e[0]] if e else text[j:]
                code_text = code_text.strip("\n")
                (container if not in_brief else result_brief).append(
                    ("codeblock" if lname == "code" else "verbatim", code_text, lang)
                    if lname == "code" else ("verbatim", code_text)
                )
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("htmlonly", "manonly", "latexonly", "rtfonly", "xmlonly", "docbookonly"):
                flush_para()
                endcmd = "end" + lname
                e = self._find_command(text, endcmd, cend)
                inner_text = text[cend:e[0]] if e else text[cend:]
                fmt = lname[:-4]
                inner = [("para", self._inline(inner_text))] if inner_text.strip() else []
                (container if not in_brief else result_brief).append(("only", {fmt}, inner))
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("endcode", "endverbatim") or lname.startswith("end") and lname in KNOWN_COMMANDS:
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in ("internal",):
                flush_para()
                e = self._find_command(text, "endinternal", cend)
                inner_text = text[cend:e[0]] if e else text[cend:]
                show = self.cfg is not None and self.cfg.get_bool("INTERNAL_DOCS")
                if show:
                    current_para_text.append(inner_text)
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("cond", "if", "ifnot"):
                # Condition name is the next word; content is shown when
                # the section is enabled (cond with no name / if section).
                flush_para()
                w, j = _read_word(text, cend)
                enabled = []
                if self.cfg is not None:
                    try:
                        enabled = self.cfg.get_list("ENABLED_SECTIONS")
                    except Exception:
                        enabled = []
                show = (w in enabled) if lname != "ifnot" else (w not in enabled)
                if lname == "cond" and not w:
                    show = False
                # Find matching end (no nesting support beyond depth count).
                e = self._find_end_cond(text, j)
                inner_text = text[j:e[0]] if e else ""
                if show:
                    sub = self._parse_blocks(inner_text, doc, allow_brief=False)
                    container.extend(sub.get("detailed", []))
                    result_brief.extend(sub.pop("brief", []))

                continue
            if lname in ("else", "elif", "endif", "endcond", "endinternal", "hideinitializer", "showinit", "hideinit", "callgraph", "callergraph", "hidecallgraph", "hidecallergraph", "inheritancegraph", "hideinheritancegraph", "tableofcontents"):
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in STRUCTURAL_COMMANDS or lname in ("ingroup", "name", "memberof", "overload"):
                # Consume to end of line.
                _, pos = _read_line(text, cend)
                continue
            if lname in ("anchor", "addindex", "lineinfo"):
                _, pos = _read_word(text, cend)
                continue
            if lname in ("image",):
                flush_para()
                line, pos_new = _read_line(text, cend)
                parts = line.split()

                    (container if not in_brief else result_brief).append(
                        ("image", parts[0], parts[1], " ".join(parts[2:]))

                continue

                flush_para()
                endcmd = {"dot": "enddot", "msc": "endmsc", "startuml": "enduml"}[lname]

                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue

                _, pos = _read_line(text, cend)
                continue
            if lname in ("li", "arg"):
                flush_para()
                # Treat as a new paragraph in a list-ish fashion.
                pos = cend
                continue
            # Not a block command: let inline parser handle from cstart.
            current_para_text.append("")  # keep text from cstart in flow below
            # Append the raw command start to current para and continue
            # scanning from there as plain text up to next interesting.
            # We do this by moving pos to cstart and finding the next
            # *block* command after it.
            nxt = self._next_block_cmd(text, cstart + 1)
            if nxt is None:
                current_para_text.append(text[cstart:])
                pos = n
            else:
                current_para_text.append(text[cstart:nxt[0]])
                pos = nxt[0]

                # to avoid losing it, set a flag: simply continue, the
                # next iteration finds it at pos because _next_interesting
                # scans from pos.
                continue

        # via _implicit_brief; here we only mark it on the doc.
        return {"brief": result_brief, "detailed": root}

    def _next_interesting(self, text, pos):
        """Find next paragraph break or command occurrence.
        Returns (kind, start, end, cmd_name_or_None)."""
        n = len(text)
        i = pos
        while i < n:
            if text[i] == "\n":
                # Check for a blank line (possibly with spaces).
                j = i + 1
                while j < n and text[j] in " \t":
                    j += 1
                if j >= n or text[j] == "\n":
                    return ("parbreak", i, j + 1 if j < n else j, None)
                i += 1
                continue
            if text[i] in "@\\" and i + 1 < n and (text[i + 1].isalpha()):
                m = CMD_RE.match(text, i)
                if m:
                    return ("cmd", i, m.end(), m.group(1))
            i += 1
        return None

    def _next_block_cmd(self, text, pos):
        i = pos
        n = len(text)
        while i < n:
            if text[i] == "\n":
                j = i + 1
                while j < n and text[j] in " \t":
                    j += 1
                if j >= n or text[j] == "\n":
                    return (i, None)
            if text[i] in "@\\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1].isalpha():
                m = CMD_RE.match(text, i)
                if m:
                    return (i, m.group(1))
            i += 1
        return None

    def _find_command(self, text, name, start):
        pat = re.compile(r"[@\\]" + re.escape(name) + r"\b")
        m = pat.search(text, start)
        if m:
            return (m.start(), m.end())
        return None

    def _find_end_cond(self, text, start):
        m = self._find_command(text, "endcond", start)
        if m:
            return m
        return self._find_command(text, "endif", start)

    def _paragraph_to_blocks(self, txt):
        # Doxygen/Markdown lists: lines starting with "- " or "-# " or "* " or "1."
        lines = txt.split("\n")
        first = lines[0].lstrip() if lines else ""
        md = self.cfg is None or self.cfg.get_bool("MARKDOWN_SUPPORT")
        list_marker = re.compile(r"^(\s*)([-*+]|(-#)|(\d+)[.)])\s+(.*)$")
        if md and any(list_marker.match(ln) for ln in lines):
            items = []
            cur = None
            ordered = False
            preamble = []
            for ln in lines:
                mm = list_marker.match(ln)
                if mm:
                    if mm.group(4):
                        ordered = True
                    if cur is not None:
                        items.append([("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur)))])
                    cur = [mm.group(5)]
                elif cur is not None:
                    cur.append(ln.strip())
                else:
                    preamble.append(ln)
            if cur is not None:
                items.append([("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur)))])
            blocks = []
            if preamble and "\n".join(preamble).strip():
                blocks.append(("para", self._inline("\n".join(preamble))))
            if items:
                blocks.append(("list", ordered, items))
            return blocks
        # Markdown heading within a paragraph (# Heading) at line start.
        if md and first.startswith("#"):
            blocks = []
            cur_lines = []
            for ln in txt.split("\n"):
                mh = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$", ln)
                if mh:
                    if cur_lines and "\n".join(cur_lines).strip():
                        blocks.append(("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur_lines))))
                        cur_lines = []
                    title = mh.group(2).strip()
                    blocks.append(("heading", len(mh.group(1)), "", self._inline(title)))
                else:
                    cur_lines.append(ln)
            if cur_lines and "\n".join(cur_lines).strip():
                blocks.append(("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur_lines))))
            return blocks
        return [("para", self._inline(txt))]

    # -- handling of line-comment single-paragraph rule is in parse() via
    # post-processing the "single-para-all" marker below.
    def _apply_single_para(self, doc):
        pass


def _split_first_sentence(nodes):
    """Split inline nodes at the first '. ' sentence end (best effort).
    Returns (first_nodes, rest_nodes) or (None, None)."""
    for idx, node in enumerate(nodes):
        if node[0] == "text":
            m = re.search(r"([.!?])(\s)", node[1])
            if m:
                first_nodes = list(nodes[:idx]) + [("text", node[1][:m.start() + 1])]
                rest_text = node[1][m.end():]
                rest_nodes = ([("text", rest_text)] if rest_text else []) + list(nodes[idx + 1:])
                return first_nodes, rest_nodes
            if node[1].rstrip().endswith((".", "!", "?")) and idx + 1 < len(nodes):
                return list(nodes[:idx + 1]), list(nodes[idx + 1:])
    return None, None

# subclass-free post hook: we intercept by wrapping the original method.
_orig_parse = DocParser.parse


def _parse_with_single_para(self, text, style="block", trailing=False):
    doc = _orig_parse(self, text, style, trailing)
    return doc


# Instead of wrapping, patch _implicit_brief consumers: the parse() above
# returns 'single-para-all' only through _implicit_brief; handle it here
# by re-implementing the tail of parse when needed.  The simplest correct
# approach: if mode would be single-para-all and there is exactly one
# detailed paragraph block, move it to brief; if there are multiple
# paragraphs and MULTILINE_CPP_IS_BRIEF is off, leave as detailed.
def _patched_parse(self, text, style="block", trailing=False):
    doc = _orig_parse(self, text, style, trailing)
    if not doc.brief and doc.detailed and style in ("line", "lineqt"):
        if not doc.is_brief_explicit:
            cfg = self.cfg
            autos = cfg is not None and (cfg.get_bool("JAVADOC_AUTOBRIEF") or cfg.get_bool("QT_AUTOBRIEF"))
            if not autos:
                if len(doc.detailed) == 1 and doc.detailed[0][0] in ("para", "list"):
                    doc.brief, doc.detailed = doc.detailed, []
    return doc


DocParser.parse = _patched_parse

class Doc:
    def __init__(self):
        self.brief = []      # list of blocks
        self.detailed = []   # list of blocks
        self.inbody = []
        self.structural = None   # (command, args string)
        self.ingroups = []

    def text_of(self, which="brief"):

def inline_to_text(nodes):
    out = []
    for n in nodes:
        tag = n[0]
        if tag == "text":
            out.append(n[1])
        elif tag == "code":
            out.append(n[1])
        elif tag in ("bold", "emph"):
            out.append(inline_to_text(n[1]))
        elif tag == "ref":
            out.append(inline_to_text(n[2]) if len(n) > 2 and n[2] else n[1])
        elif tag == "link":
            out.append(inline_to_text(n[2]))
        elif tag == "break":
            out.append("\n")
    return "".join(out)


def blocks_to_text(blocks):
    out = []
    for b in blocks:
        tag = b[0]
        if tag == "para":
            out.append(inline_to_text(b[1]))
        elif tag == "simplesect":
            out.append(blocks_to_text(b[2]))
        elif tag == "paramlist":
            for names, desc in b[2]:
                out.append(blocks_to_text(desc))
        elif tag in ("codeblock", "verbatim"):
            out.append(b[1])
        elif tag == "list":
            for item in b[2]:
                out.append(blocks_to_text(item))
        elif tag == "sect":
            out.append(inline_to_text(b[3]))
            out.append(blocks_to_text(b[4]))
        elif tag == "only":
            out.append(blocks_to_text(b[2]))

def _read_word(text, i):
    """Read the next whitespace-delimited word; return (word, new_index)."""
    n = len(text)
    while i < n and text[i] in " \t":
        i += 1
    start = i
    while i < n and text[i] not in " \t\n":
        i += 1
    return text[start:i], i


def _read_line(text, i):
    n = len(text)
    start = i
    while i < n and text[i] != "\n":
        i += 1
    return text[start:i], i


class _InlineParser:
    def __init__(self, text, warn, fileline):
        self.text = text
        self.warn = warn
        self.fileline = fileline  # (file, start_line)

    def warn_unknown(self, cmd, pos):
        if self.warn:
            line = self.fileline[1] + self.text[:pos].count("\n")
            self.warn(
                f"{self.fileline[0]}:{line}: warning: Found unknown command '{cmd}'\n"
            )

    def parse(self, start=0, end=None, stop_cmd=None):
        """Parse inline content.  Returns (nodes, index) where index is at
        the stopping command/paragraph end if any."""
        text = self.text
        n = len(text) if end is None else end
        nodes = []
        buf = []

        def flush():
            if buf:
                nodes.append(("text", "".join(buf)))
                buf.clear()

        i = start
        while i < n:
            ch = text[i]
            if ch in "@\\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1].isalpha():
                m = CMD_RE.match(text, i)
                if m:
                    cmd = m.group(1).lower()
                    cmd_text = text[i:m.end()]
                    if stop_cmd and cmd == stop_cmd:
                        flush()
                        return nodes, i
                    if cmd in ("c", "p"):
                        flush()
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        nodes.append(("code", word.strip(".,;:") if word.endswith(".") and cmd == "p" else word))
                        # The punctuation handling above is intentionally
                        # simple; see below for the '.' that trails a \p.
                        if word.endswith("."):

                            # word was 'paramref.' at the end of a sentence.
                            pass
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "b":
                        flush()
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        nodes.append(("bold", [("text", word)]))
                        continue
                    elif cmd in ("e", "em", "a"):
                        flush()
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        nodes.append(("emph", [("text", word)]))
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "n":
                        flush()
                        nodes.append(("break",))
                        i = m.end()
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "ref":
                        flush()
                        # \ref target ["text"]
                        j = m.end()
                        while j < n and text[j] in " \t":
                            j += 1
                        if j < n and text[j] == '"':
                            # \ref "text" form is not standard; treat word.
                            pass
                        target, j = _read_word(text, j)
                        # Optional quoted display text.
                        k = j
                        while k < n and text[k] in " \t":
                            k += 1
                        display = None
                        if k < n and text[k] == '"':
                            e = text.find('"', k + 1)
                            if e != -1 and e <= n:
                                display = text[k + 1:e]
                                j = e + 1
                        nodes.append(("ref", target, [("text", display)] if display else None))
                        i = j
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "link":
                        flush()
                        target, j = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        inner, j2 = self.parse(j, n, stop_cmd="endlink")
                        nodes.append(("ref", target, inner))
                        i = j2
                        continue
                    elif cmd == "endlink":
                        flush()
                        return nodes, i
                    elif cmd == "emoji":
                        word, i = _read_word(text, m.end())
                        buf.append(f":{word}:")
                        continue
                    elif cmd in KNOWN_COMMANDS:
                        # A known command that is not handled inline;
                        # let the block parser deal with it by stopping.
                        flush()
                        return nodes, i
                    else:
                        self.warn_unknown(cmd_text, i)
                        buf.append(cmd_text)
                        i = m.end()
                        continue
            if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < n and not text[i + 1].isalpha():
                # Escaped special character.
                buf.append(text[i + 1])
                i += 2
                continue
            if ch == "@" and i + 1 < n and not text[i + 1].isalpha():
                buf.append(text[i + 1] if text[i + 1] in "@\\$&%\"#." else "@")
                i += 2 if text[i + 1] in "@\\$&%\"#." else 1
                continue
            buf.append(ch)
            i += 1
        flush()
        return nodes, i


def parse_inline(text, warn=None, fileline=("", 1)):
    return _InlineParser(text, warn, fileline).parse(0)[0]


def _split_paragraphs(text):
    """Split text into paragraph strings separated by blank lines."""
    paras = []
    cur = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if line.strip() == "":
            if cur:
                paras.append("\n".join(cur))
                cur = []
        else:
            cur.append(line)
    if cur:
        paras.append("\n".join(cur))
    return paras


def apply_markdown_inline(nodes):
    """Apply lightweight Markdown emphasis/code/link processing to text
    nodes (used both for Markdown files and markup in comments)."""
    out = []
    for node in nodes:
        if node[0] != "text":
            out.append(node)
            continue
        s = node[1]
        # Process `code`, **bold**, *emph*, [text](url) in a single scan.
        i = 0
        buf = []

        def flush():
            if buf:
                out.append(("text", "".join(buf)))
                buf.clear()

        while i < len(s):
            if s.startswith("`", i):
                j = s.find("`", i + 1)
                if j != -1:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("code", s[i + 1:j]))
                    i = j + 1
                    continue
            if s.startswith("**", i) or s.startswith("__", i):
                marker = s[i:i + 2]
                j = s.find(marker, i + 2)
                if j != -1:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("bold", [("text", s[i + 2:j])]))
                    i = j + 2
                    continue
            if s[i] in "*_" and i + 1 < len(s) and not s[i + 1].isspace():
                j = s.find(s[i], i + 1)
                if j != -1 and j > i + 1:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("emph", [("text", s[i + 1:j])]))
                    i = j + 1
                    continue
            if s[i] == "[":
                m = re.match(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)\s]+)[^)]*\)", s[i:])
                if m:
                    flush()
                    out.append(("link", m.group(2), [("text", m.group(1))]))
                    i += m.end()
                    continue
            buf.append(s[i])
            i += 1
        flush()
    return out


class DocParser:
    def __init__(self, cfg, warn=None, filename="", start_line=1):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.warn = warn
        self.filename = filename
        self.start_line = start_line

    def _warn(self, msg):
        if self.warn:
            self.warn(msg)

    def _inline(self, text):
        idx_parser = _InlineParser(text, self._warn,
                                    (self.filename, self.start_line))
        nodes, _ = idx_parser.parse(0)
        if self.cfg is None or self.cfg.get_bool("MARKDOWN_SUPPORT"):
            nodes = apply_markdown_inline(nodes)
        # Merge adjacent text nodes and normalise whitespace runs
        # (keeping single spaces).
        merged = []
        for node in nodes:
            if node[0] == "text":
                txt = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", node[1])
                if merged and merged[-1][0] == "text":
                    merged[-1] = ("text", merged[-1][1] + txt)
                else:
                    merged.append(("text", txt))
            else:
                merged.append(node)
        return merged

    def parse(self, text, style="block", trailing=False):
        """style: one of 'block', 'line', 'qt', 'lineqt', 'python'."""
        doc = Doc()
        original = text
        text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

        # Extract \ingroup commands (removing them from the text).
        def repl_ingroup(m):
            doc.ingroups.extend(m.group(1).split())
            return ""
        text = re.sub(r"[@\\]ingroup\s+([^\n]*)", repl_ingroup, text)
        text = re.sub(r"[@\\]memberof\s+([^\n]*)", "", text)

        # Structural command: only when it is the first command in the block.
        stripped = text.lstrip(" \t\n")
        m = CMD_RE.match(stripped)
        if m and m.group(1).lower() in STRUCTURAL_COMMANDS:
            cmd = m.group(1).lower()
            rest, _ = _read_line(stripped, m.end())
            doc.structural = (cmd, rest.strip())
            # Remove the command and its line-rest from the text.
            first_nl = stripped.find("\n", m.end())
            if first_nl == -1:
                text = ""
            else:
                text = stripped[first_nl + 1:]
            if cmd == "defgroup" or cmd in ("addtogroup", "weakgroup"):
                pass

        doc.has_doc = bool(original.strip()) or doc.structural is not None

        # Determine explicit brief.
        has_brief = bool(re.search(r"[@\\](brief|short)\b", text))

        blocks_detailed = []
        blocks_brief = []

        # Tokenise by paragraphs, but block commands may start mid
        # paragraph.  We walk the whole text with a state machine over
        # "segments": (text chunk between block commands).
        detailed = self._parse_blocks(text, doc, allow_brief=has_brief)
        blocks_brief = detailed.pop("brief", [])
        blocks_detailed = detailed.get("detailed", [])

        # Implicit brief handling.
        if not has_brief and not blocks_brief:
            mode = self._implicit_brief(style, trailing)
            if mode == "all":
                blocks_brief, blocks_detailed = blocks_detailed, []
            elif mode == "first-para" and blocks_detailed:
                if blocks_detailed[0][0] == "para":
                    blocks_brief = [blocks_detailed.pop(0)]
            elif mode == "first-sentence" and blocks_detailed:
                if blocks_detailed[0][0] == "para":
                    first, rest = _split_first_sentence(blocks_detailed[0][1])
                    if first is not None and rest is not None:
                        blocks_brief = [("para", first)]
                        if rest:
                            blocks_detailed[0] = ("para", rest)
                        else:
                            blocks_detailed.pop(0)
                    else:
                        blocks_brief = [blocks_detailed.pop(0)]

        doc.brief = blocks_brief
        doc.detailed = blocks_detailed
        return doc

    def _implicit_brief(self, style, trailing):
        cfg = self.cfg
        if cfg is None:
            return "all" if style in ("line", "lineqt") and not trailing else None
        javadoc = cfg.get_bool("JAVADOC_AUTOBRIEF")
        qt = cfg.get_bool("QT_AUTOBRIEF")
        is_qt_style = style in ("qt", "lineqt")
        is_javadoc_style = style in ("block", "line")
        if javadoc or qt:
            if (is_javadoc_style and javadoc) or (is_qt_style and qt):
                return "first-sentence"
            return None
        if style in ("line", "lineqt"):
            if cfg.get_bool("MULTILINE_CPP_IS_BRIEF"):
                return "first-para"
            return "single-para-all"
        return None

    def _parse_blocks(self, text, doc, allow_brief):
        """Returns {"brief": [...], "detailed": [...]}."""
        result_brief = []
        root = []

        # Current insertion point for paragraphs: a list in `containers`.
        current_para_text = []
        container = root            # list to append new blocks to
        in_brief = False
        brief_done = False
        # For param/simple sections: the container is the item's desc list.
        container_stack = []

        def flush_para():
            nonlocal current_para_text
            txt = "".join(current_para_text).strip("\n")
            current_para_text = []
            if txt.strip() == "":
                return
            # A paragraph may itself be a Markdown/doxygen list.
            blocks = self._paragraph_to_blocks(txt)
            target = result_brief if in_brief else container
            target.extend(blocks)

        # Walk line by line, detecting block commands at token level.
        # We process the text as a stream, breaking on commands.
        pos = 0
        n = len(text)
        # Pre-scan for verbatim/code blocks and replace with markers?
        # Simpler: handle them when the command is encountered at the
        # start of a segment below.

        while pos < n:
            # Find next command that *starts a block* or an end of paragraph.
            m = self._next_interesting(text, pos)
            if m is None:
                current_para_text.append(text[pos:])
                pos = n
                break
            kind, cstart, cend, cmd = m
            if kind == "parbreak":
                current_para_text.append(text[pos:cstart])
                flush_para()
                # A blank line ends a \brief paragraph.
                if in_brief:
                    in_brief = False
                    brief_done = True
                pos = cend
                continue
            # kind == 'cmd'
            current_para_text.append(text[pos:cstart])
            lname = cmd.lower()
            if lname in ("brief", "short"):
                flush_para()
                if not brief_done:
                    in_brief = True
                    doc.is_brief_explicit = True
                else:
                    # Subsequent \brief becomes a detailed paragraph.
                    in_brief = False
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in ("details", "detail"):
                flush_para()
                in_brief = False
                brief_done = True
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in ("param", "tparam", "retval", "exception", "throw", "throws"):
                flush_para()
                in_brief = False
                if lname == "param":
                    # \param[dir] name[,name] description
                    j = cend
                    while j < n and text[j] in " \t":
                        j += 1
                    direction = None
                    if j < n and text[j] == "[":
                        e = text.find("]", j)
                        if e != -1:
                            direction = text[j + 1:e].strip()
                            j = e + 1
                    names = []
                    while True:
                        w, j2 = _read_word(text, j)
                        if not w:
                            break
                        names.extend([x for x in re.split(r",", w) if x])
                        j = j2
                        # comma separated more names?
                        k = j
                        while k < n and text[k] in " \t":
                            k += 1
                        if k < n and text[k] == ",":
                            j = k + 1
                            continue
                        break
                    kind_list = "param"
                    pos = j
                else:
                    w, pos = _read_word(text, cend)
                    names = [w] if w else []
                    kind_list = {
                        "tparam": "templateparam",
                        "retval": "retval",
                        "exception": "exception",
                        "throw": "exception",
                        "throws": "exception",
                    }[lname]
                    direction = None
                # Find existing trailing paramlist of same kind to append.
                target = container if container is not None else root
                # Close any simplesect container first.
                if container_stack:
                    while container_stack:
                        container = container_stack.pop()
                    target = container
                if target and target[-1][0] == "paramlist" and target[-1][1] == kind_list:
                    plist = target[-1][2]
                else:
                    plist = []
                    target.append(("paramlist", kind_list, plist))
                desc = []
                named = [(nm, direction) for nm in names] if direction else [(nm, None) for nm in names]
                plist.append((named, desc))
                container_stack.append(target)
                container = desc
                continue
            if lname in SIMPLESECT_KINDS:
                flush_para()
                in_brief = False
                kind_sect = SIMPLESECT_KINDS[lname]
                if container_stack:
                    while container_stack:
                        container = container_stack.pop()
                target = container
                inner = []
                target.append(("simplesect", kind_sect, inner))
                container_stack.append(target)
                container = inner
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in ("section", "subsection", "subsubsection", "paragraph"):
                flush_para()
                in_brief = False
                level = {"section": 1, "subsection": 2, "subsubsection": 3, "paragraph": 4}[lname]
                sid, j = _read_word(text, cend)
                title, j2 = _read_line(text, j)
                if not sid and title:
                    sid = ""
                if container_stack:
                    while container_stack:
                        container = container_stack.pop()
                inner = []
                container.append(("sect", level, sid, self._inline(title.strip()), inner))
                container_stack.append(container)
                container = inner
                pos = j2
                continue
            if lname in ("code", "verbatim"):
                flush_para()
                endcmd = "endcode" if lname == "code" else "endverbatim"
                # Optional {language} or .ext after \code
                j = cend
                lang = ""
                mj = re.match(r"\s*\{([^}]*)\}|\s*\.([A-Za-z0-9_]+)", text[j:j+40])
                if mj:
                    lang = mj.group(1) or mj.group(2) or ""
                    j += mj.end()
                e = self._find_command(text, endcmd, j)
                code_text = text[j:e[0]] if e else text[j:]
                code_text = code_text.strip("\n")
                (container if not in_brief else result_brief).append(
                    ("codeblock" if lname == "code" else "verbatim", code_text, lang)
                    if lname == "code" else ("verbatim", code_text)
                )
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("htmlonly", "manonly", "latexonly", "rtfonly", "xmlonly", "docbookonly"):
                flush_para()
                endcmd = "end" + lname
                e = self._find_command(text, endcmd, cend)
                inner_text = text[cend:e[0]] if e else text[cend:]
                fmt = lname[:-4]
                inner = [("para", self._inline(inner_text))] if inner_text.strip() else []
                (container if not in_brief else result_brief).append(("only", {fmt}, inner))
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("endcode", "endverbatim") or lname.startswith("end") and lname in KNOWN_COMMANDS:
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in ("internal",):
                flush_para()
                e = self._find_command(text, "endinternal", cend)
                inner_text = text[cend:e[0]] if e else text[cend:]
                show = self.cfg is not None and self.cfg.get_bool("INTERNAL_DOCS")
                if show:
                    current_para_text.append(inner_text)
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("cond", "if", "ifnot"):
                # Condition name is the next word; content is shown when
                # the section is enabled (cond with no name / if section).
                flush_para()
                w, j = _read_word(text, cend)
                enabled = []
                if self.cfg is not None:
                    try:
                        enabled = self.cfg.get_list("ENABLED_SECTIONS")
                    except Exception:
                        enabled = []
                show = (w in enabled) if lname != "ifnot" else (w not in enabled)
                if lname == "cond" and not w:
                    show = False
                # Find matching end (no nesting support beyond depth count).
                e = self._find_end_cond(text, j)
                inner_text = text[j:e[0]] if e else ""
                if show:
                    sub = self._parse_blocks(inner_text, doc, allow_brief=False)
                    container.extend(sub.get("detailed", []))
                    result_brief.extend(sub.pop("brief", []))
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("else", "elif", "endif", "endcond", "endinternal", "hideinitializer", "showinit", "hideinit", "callgraph", "callergraph", "hidecallgraph", "hidecallergraph", "inheritancegraph", "hideinheritancegraph", "tableofcontents"):
                pos = cend
                continue
            if lname in STRUCTURAL_COMMANDS or lname in ("ingroup", "name", "memberof", "overload"):
                # Consume to end of line.
                _, pos = _read_line(text, cend)
                continue
            if lname in ("anchor", "addindex", "lineinfo"):
                _, pos = _read_word(text, cend)
                continue
            if lname in ("image",):
                flush_para()
                line, pos_new = _read_line(text, cend)
                parts = line.split()
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    (container if not in_brief else result_brief).append(
                        ("image", parts[0], parts[1], " ".join(parts[2:]))
                    )
                pos = pos_new
                continue
            if lname in ("dot", "msc", "startuml"):
                flush_para()
                endcmd = {"dot": "enddot", "msc": "endmsc", "startuml": "enduml"}[lname]
                e = self._find_command(text, endcmd, cend)
                pos = e[1] if e else n
                continue
            if lname in ("include", "includelineno", "snippet", "dontinclude"):
                _, pos = _read_line(text, cend)
                continue
            if lname in ("li", "arg"):
                flush_para()
                # Treat as a new paragraph in a list-ish fashion.
                pos = cend
                continue
            # Not a block command: let inline parser handle from cstart.
            current_para_text.append("")  # keep text from cstart in flow below
            # Append the raw command start to current para and continue
            # scanning from there as plain text up to next interesting.
            # We do this by moving pos to cstart and finding the next
            # *block* command after it.
            nxt = self._next_block_cmd(text, cstart + 1)
            if nxt is None:
                current_para_text.append(text[cstart:])
                pos = n
            else:
                current_para_text.append(text[cstart:nxt[0]])
                pos = nxt[0]
                # Loop will process the command at pos by re-detecting;
                # to avoid losing it, set a flag: simply continue, the
                # next iteration finds it at pos because _next_interesting
                # scans from pos.
                continue

        flush_para()
        # single-para-all handling for line comments is decided by caller
        # via _implicit_brief; here we only mark it on the doc.
        return {"brief": result_brief, "detailed": root}

    def _next_interesting(self, text, pos):
        """Find next paragraph break or command occurrence.
        Returns (kind, start, end, cmd_name_or_None)."""
        n = len(text)
        i = pos
        while i < n:
            if text[i] == "\n":
                # Check for a blank line (possibly with spaces).
                j = i + 1
                while j < n and text[j] in " \t":
                    j += 1
                if j >= n or text[j] == "\n":
                    return ("parbreak", i, j + 1 if j < n else j, None)
                i += 1
                continue
            if text[i] in "@\\" and i + 1 < n and (text[i + 1].isalpha()):
                m = CMD_RE.match(text, i)
                if m:
                    return ("cmd", i, m.end(), m.group(1))
            i += 1
        return None

    def _next_block_cmd(self, text, pos):
        i = pos
        n = len(text)
        while i < n:
            if text[i] == "\n":
                j = i + 1
                while j < n and text[j] in " \t":
                    j += 1
                if j >= n or text[j] == "\n":
                    return (i, None)
            if text[i] in "@\\" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1].isalpha():
                m = CMD_RE.match(text, i)
                if m:
                    return (i, m.group(1))
            i += 1
        return None

    def _find_command(self, text, name, start):
        pat = re.compile(r"[@\\]" + re.escape(name) + r"\b")
        m = pat.search(text, start)
        if m:
            return (m.start(), m.end())
        return None

    def _find_end_cond(self, text, start):
        m = self._find_command(text, "endcond", start)
        if m:
            return m
        return self._find_command(text, "endif", start)

    def _paragraph_to_blocks(self, txt):
        # Doxygen/Markdown lists: lines starting with "- " or "-# " or "* " or "1."
        lines = txt.split("\n")
        first = lines[0].lstrip() if lines else ""
        md = self.cfg is None or self.cfg.get_bool("MARKDOWN_SUPPORT")
        list_marker = re.compile(r"^(\s*)([-*+]|(-#)|(\d+)[.)])\s+(.*)$")
        if md and any(list_marker.match(ln) for ln in lines):
            items = []
            cur = None
            ordered = False
            preamble = []
            for ln in lines:
                mm = list_marker.match(ln)
                if mm:
                    if mm.group(4):
                        ordered = True
                    if cur is not None:
                        items.append([("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur)))])
                    cur = [mm.group(5)]
                elif cur is not None:
                    cur.append(ln.strip())
                else:
                    preamble.append(ln)
            if cur is not None:
                items.append([("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur)))])
            blocks = []
            if preamble and "\n".join(preamble).strip():
                blocks.append(("para", self._inline("\n".join(preamble))))
            if items:
                blocks.append(("list", ordered, items))
            return blocks
        # Markdown heading within a paragraph (# Heading) at line start.
        if md and first.startswith("#"):
            blocks = []
            cur_lines = []
            for ln in txt.split("\n"):
                mh = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$", ln)
                if mh:
                    if cur_lines and "\n".join(cur_lines).strip():
                        blocks.append(("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur_lines))))
                        cur_lines = []
                    title = mh.group(2).strip()
                    blocks.append(("heading", len(mh.group(1)), "", self._inline(title)))
                else:
                    cur_lines.append(ln)
            if cur_lines and "\n".join(cur_lines).strip():
                blocks.append(("para", self._inline("\n".join(cur_lines))))
            return blocks
        return [("para", self._inline(txt))]

    # -- handling of line-comment single-paragraph rule is in parse() via
    # post-processing the "single-para-all" marker below.
    def _apply_single_para(self, doc):

def _split_first_sentence(nodes):
    """Split inline nodes at the first '. ' sentence end (best effort).
    Returns (first_nodes, rest_nodes) or (None, None)."""
    for idx, node in enumerate(nodes):
        if node[0] == "text":
            m = re.search(r"([.!?])(\s)", node[1])
            if m:
                first_nodes = list(nodes[:idx]) + [("text", node[1][:m.start() + 1])]
                rest_text = node[1][m.end():]
                rest_nodes = ([("text", rest_text)] if rest_text else []) + list(nodes[idx + 1:])
                return first_nodes, rest_nodes
            if node[1].rstrip().endswith((".", "!", "?")) and idx + 1 < len(nodes):
                return list(nodes[:idx + 1]), list(nodes[idx + 1:])
    return None, None

# subclass-free post hook: we intercept by wrapping the original method.
_orig_parse = DocParser.parse


def _parse_with_single_para(self, text, style="block", trailing=False):
    doc = _orig_parse(self, text, style, trailing)
    return doc


# Instead of wrapping, patch _implicit_brief consumers: the parse() above
# returns 'single-para-all' only through _implicit_brief; handle it here
# by re-implementing the tail of parse when needed.  The simplest correct
# approach: if mode would be single-para-all and there is exactly one
# detailed paragraph block, move it to brief; if there are multiple
# paragraphs and MULTILINE_CPP_IS_BRIEF is off, leave as detailed.
def _patched_parse(self, text, style="block", trailing=False):
    doc = _orig_parse(self, text, style, trailing)
    if not doc.brief and doc.detailed and style in ("line", "lineqt"):
        if not doc.is_brief_explicit:
            cfg = self.cfg
            autos = cfg is not None and (cfg.get_bool("JAVADOC_AUTOBRIEF") or cfg.get_bool("QT_AUTOBRIEF"))
            if not autos:
                if len(doc.detailed) == 1 and doc.detailed[0][0] in ("para", "list"):
                    doc.brief, doc.detailed = doc.detailed, []
    return doc
